result.title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
result.summary: Designing healthcare strategies requires anticipating their clinical and operational consequences before implementation, a task that often relies on health system simulation. Such a simulation necessitates modeling how patient states evolve and generate care demands. However, conventional approaches typically tailor compact state transitions to a single policy question and omit history-dependent dynamics, thus requiring the redefinition of states and transitions when there is a new question that entails different clinical information. We propose to learn a patient world model from longitudinal EHRs using a neural network to provide a shared clinical representation of patient trajectories that can serve simulation questions across scenarios. Taking ICU operations as an example, we train the model on MIMIC-IV, freeze it, and couple its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues via scenario-specific mappings, so that one model renders admission demand, care tasks, and discharge proposals across simulations evaluating ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity. Experiments show that our model matches Markov and semi-Markov comparators in aggregate occupancy and directional responses to capacity and dispatch policies. It also reproduces policy gains from replayed observed trajectories. For patients entering the same support state from different prior trajectories, the learned representation captures a 24-h recovery difference (-6.4 predicted versus -6.7 observed percentage points), a contrast missed by compact state models, which propagates into distinct simulated care demand, queue burden, and bed use. These results indicate that a learned world model of patient dynamics has the potential to replace question-specific state models, allowing new care policies to be evaluated by reconfiguring the scenario without model rebuilding.

AI.brief_summary: 该文从纵向 EHR 中学习 ICU 患者的「世界模型」，用神经网络给出可跨场景复用的患者轨迹表示，冻结后经场景映射接入床位、护理调度与转出资源，模拟入院需求、护理任务与出院建议。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关联，但其「紧凑状态是否会丢失轨迹依赖信息」的对比（相同支持状态、不同历史导致约 24 小时恢复差异）可供核查 latent 推理状态应保留多少历史与任务必要信息、以及状态表示能否跨问题复用。
